title: The normalized root map into the integral line
statement: For prime ell, any scheme X, and any finite subextension E of the fixed algebraic closure, there exists IntegralRoots ell E X of [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-diagrams]. Its map from the actual root-tower limit to the underlying integral twist has, at each positive level, exactly the root-limit projection followed by the free-module unit. Thus the map is determined by these projections. Any two such IntegralRoots are equal.

proof.text: At level n, use the root projection followed by the free-module unit. Naturality of that unit for the tensor of the coefficient transition and the root power map proves compatibility with consecutive levels.
Forget the fixed integral module scalar action. This functor preserves limits; its limiting cone lifts the compatible root projections and gives all required equations.

mathlib_searches.query: A cone of root projections followed by free module units induces a map into the inverse limit of integral Tate twists. Coefficient quotient by a regular element commutes with geometric pullback and direct image.
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits concerning adic-completion projections, perfectoid untilts, and inverse limits; no diagonal root-cone or scalar/pullback compatibility theorem.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Use the ordinary limit universal property and the existing free-module adjunction.

mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits, including isLimitOfPreserves and preserves_lift_mapCone. isLimitOfPreserves gives exactly the underlying-module limit used by the root map.
